name: Docker Agent

hlido_opinion.headline: Agents defined in YAML and run like containers — a clean, developer-honest tool from Docker with first-class CLI, HTTP API, MCP and A2A, let down only by what a docs read cannot verify.
hlido_opinion.body: Docker Agent applies the container mental model to AI agents: declare an agent (model, instruction, toolsets, teammates) in a YAML or HCL file, run it with one command, and share it through any OCI registry — the same workflow developers already use for images. The documentation is excellent and refreshingly honest about scope: it states plainly what the tool is (a CLI that runs declarative agents) and what it isn't (not a framework you write code in, not a hosted SaaS, not a model), and backs the no-glue-code claim with a concrete before/after that replaces ~30 lines of SDK plumbing with an eight-line YAML. For the agent-to-agent world this is about as well-positioned as a runtime gets: TUI, CLI, HTTP API, MCP server, A2A, OCI distribution, multi-agent delegation and any-model support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, local). It is open source and from a vendor with real distribution credibility. The score stops short of the top band only because a docs-site read cannot confirm the runtime actually behaves as described; the public surface, however, is among the strongest we have reviewed in this category.

tier_rationale: STEADY (83): exceptional documentation, a clear and honest positioning, deep agent-native surface (CLI/API/MCP/A2A/OCI) and a credible open-source vendor. Held below VITAL only because runtime behaviour was not exercised on a public-surface pass.
what_it_does_well: Declarative, no-glue-code model for defining and running agents (YAML/HCL), shown with a convincing before/after
Deep, agent-native interface surface: CLI, TUI, HTTP API, MCP server, A2A and OCI distribution
Honest, scoped positioning ('what it is / what it isn't') and documentation that flags unreleased features
Model-agnostic (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, local) and extensible via Docker's MCP catalogue
what_it_fails_at: Runtime behaviour (orchestration loop, tool execution) could not be verified from a documentation read
Docs track the main branch and may describe unreleased features, so some capabilities may not yet be stable
best_for: Developers who want agents in their existing container/OCI workflow without writing orchestration glue
Teams building multi-agent setups that should be shareable and reproducible like images
Agent-to-agent integrators who need MCP, A2A and an HTTP API out of the box
not_recommended_for: Non-developers who want a no-terminal, hosted product
Teams that need a managed SaaS with a UI rather than a local CLI/runtime

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: First-class: run via CLI, call over an HTTP API, expose/consume MCP servers, delegate via A2A, and distribute agents over any OCI registry.

claims.claim: docker-agent lets you create and run intelligent AI agents that collaborate to solve complex problems — no code required.
claims.evidence: Documented with concrete YAML examples, a before/after against ~30 lines of SDK glue, and multi-agent delegation described; no application code needed to define/run an agent.

summary: Agents defined in YAML and run like containers — a clean, developer-honest tool from Docker with first-class CLI, HTTP API, MCP and A2A, let down only by what a docs read cannot verify.
